summary.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 1,693 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.53%, while volumes fell 24.5%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR 1,693 crore, up 22% YoY, despite lower volumes, driven by higher raw material prices from the West Asia conflict. Operating EBITDA rose 88% YoY to INR 331 crore (19.53% margin) and PAT was INR 236 crore (13.96% margin), helped by wide global deltas between styrene monomer and downstream products. Manufactured volumes fell 24.5% YoY to 70,842 MT, with exports nearly absent and non-OEM demand down roughly 50%. Management declined to guide on volumes or margins, calling the situation fluid, and announced polystyrene and compounding expansions plus a new 80,000 TPA PS line totaling about INR 450 crore, funded from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: Trading sales share of top line

segments.name: Polystyrene (GPPS/HIPS/EPS)
segments.commentary: OEM demand stable; non-OEM demand fell close to 50% in the quarter, partly due to high prices and downstream gas supply issues. Exports were about 10% of normal quarterly levels.

segments.name: ABS and compounding
segments.commentary: Compounding capacity to rise from 50,000 to 80,000 TPA, with lines focused on ABS compounds. ABS volumes not disclosed separately; ABS nameplate capacity to reach 140,000 TPA after full expansion.

segments.name: EPS
segments.commentary: Phase 2 EPS capacity completed, taking capacity to about 1,43,000 TPA; management said no near-term EPS expansion planned and exports have stalled.

segments.name: XPS / wide-width board
segments.commentary: New wide-width EPS/XPS board line of 150,000 cubic metres to be commissioned by June 2027.

guidance_outlook: No volume or margin guidance given; management cited fluid West Asia situation, freight, shipping and styrene availability.
Current India CFR styrene monomer around USD 1,300; Q1 range roughly USD 1,350-1,400 with peak above USD 1,500.

Current deltas: GPPS about USD 250-275/MT and HIPS about USD 350/MT, versus USD 200 for GPPS and USD 275-300 for HIPS in normal times; management said current margins are aberrational and will normalise.
Wide-width board, compounding expansion to be commissioned by June 2027; 80,000 TPA PS line at Amdoshi by December 2028; all capacities on board by March 2029.
Total capex plan close to INR 900 crore, funded from internal accruals; asset turn about 2x at full capacity.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 EPS expansion completed; EPS capacity about 1,43,000 TPA.

New wide-width EPS board line of 150,000 cubic metres, with compounding expansion from 50,000 to 80,000 TPA, to be commissioned by June 2027; estimated total cost of these projects with PS line about INR 450 crore.
New 80,000 TPA polystyrene line at Amdoshi, Maharashtra, approved by board; completion by December 2028, lifting total PS capacity from 300,000 to 380,000 TPA.
Focus areas: ABS line 2, XPS and compounding lines; Chennai expansion considered but some time away.
Management said compounds capacity should be fully sold out in 3-4 years and expanded capacity used over 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Revenue grew despite volume decline, as raw material cost inflation passed through; delta widening benefited margins.
Alternate styrene supply secured for domestic customers; exports curtailed by freight rates, longer voyages and Red Sea issues.
Management estimated about 20,000 tons of PS imports in Q1 (unofficial), attributed partly to a temporary import duty suspension; last year imports were about 87,000 tons.
Non-OEM customers reportedly reconciled to higher prices, with demand returning; management said renewed hostilities have raised styrene prices again.
Management stated the company does not supply to customers without credit discipline; competitors reportedly give 40-50 days credit.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 volume fall split between OEM and non-OEM, and what are imports doing?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-OEM demand fell close to 50%; OEM demand was stable to slightly better. Exports were about 10% of normal. Import data is no longer published; unofficial estimate about 20,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 80,000 TPA compounding expansion be absorbed, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the expanded compounding capacity to be used over 2-3 years after June 2027, with ABS compounds the main growth driver.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the profit improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from wider global deltas, not volume; management called the level an aberration that will normalise over time and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex total and does it include the XPS expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex about INR 900 crore, funded internally, and includes the 150,000 cubic metre wide-width board line.

qa_highlights.question: What is current styrene and delta pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: India CFR styrene about USD 1,300 currently, versus USD 1,350-1,400 Q1 average. Current GPPS delta about USD 250-275 and HIPS about USD 350.

qa_highlights.question: Are alternate styrene sources structurally more expensive?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; freight rates are higher because Gulf voyages took 4-7 days, while alternate sources involve longer voyages and shipping constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Did the industry de-grow in line with the company?
qa_highlights.answer: In polystyrene, management said the industry de-grew at the same rate; in EPS, the company de-grew less than the fragmented industry.

risks_watch: West Asia hostilities and shipping: freight, voyage time and styrene availability drive both volume and cost.
Import duty suspension on polymers eroding domestic market share; watch policy changes.
Non-OEM demand recovery and whether credit discipline costs volume.
Normalisation of GPPS/HIPS deltas from current levels toward historical USD 200-300 range.
Execution of INR 450 crore (and ~INR 900 crore total) capex on schedule by June 2027, December 2028 and March 2029.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the company's market position and the long-term expansion case, but cautious and non-committal on near-term volumes and margins, which management repeatedly declined to quantify.
key_quotes: It is not one plant, one source but it is a full region from where the material is not coming in and even during COVID times, this situation was not there.
A project is not set up for the temporary events of one quarter.
